metaDescription: Upright vacuums under $300 compared across one premium Dyson and light Shark and Eureka models, showing when the top of the cap pays back and when it does not.
expertTake: The Dyson Ball Animal 3 is the best upright under $300 because its 290 air watt motor and de-tangling Motorbar head are a clear step above everything else in the band. The Shark Navigator ZU561 is the value pick with a seal and a pod. Skip the Dyson if you want a bag or a light machine; it is bagless and heavy.
introParagraphs: At the top of this price cap the market splits in two. One group is the premium uprights with real engineering behind the motor and head, and the other is the same light, sensible machines that sit in the cheaper bands.

The useful question is whether the extra budget buys something you will notice: power, a head that clears hair on its own or a seal. The cap of $300 reflects listing prices when this guide was updated, and prices move, so check the current figure before you buy.

products.name: Dyson Ball Animal 3 upright, 290AW, de-tangling Motorbar
products.description:
This is the machine that justifies the top of the band. At 290 air watts it is rated well above every light upright here, a measure that combines pressure and airflow and is more meaningful than a bare pressure figure. A de-tangling Motorbar head clears wrapped hair from the bar as you clean, and three suction modes let you tune the power to the floor.

The ball steering pivots around furniture with a turn of the wrist, and Radial Root Cyclone technology increases suction. Next to the Shark ZU561 it is stronger and heavier and has no pod, and next to the Eureka NEU350 it is a different class of machine.

The cost of ownership is the bin and the filters. Empty the bin at the line into a bag held tight to the opening, wash the filters on schedule and let them dry for a full day, and clear any hair that escapes to the bearing end of the bar. Check the hose when suction seems low, because a plug in the hose is far more common than a motor fault, and keep the ball joint clear of lint so the steering stays free. The machine is heavy, so avoid carrying it up stairs with the cord attached and use the stair tool from the landing instead. Lift the head over thresholds and do not drag it backward by the cord, since the cord is the part that wears first on any corded machine. Because it has only two accessories, a pet household should price the groom tool and the turbine tool before buying, since the kit with the full set costs more than this cap allows and the missing tools are what many owners wish they had after a month.
products.bestFor: Pet homes with carpet that want a premium motor and self-clearing head.
cons: Bagless bin releases dust when emptied

products.name: Shark Navigator Lift-Away Speed ZU561, self-cleaning roll, HEPA

specList.label: Filtration
specList.value: HEPA, over 99.9 percent of dust and allergens

products.description:
The ZU561 is the value pick of the band: a self-cleaning brushroll for pet hair, a lift-away pod for stairs and a complete seal around a HEPA filter. That combination costs far less than the Dyson and solves most of the chores a pet household has.

Next to the Ball Animal 3 it is lighter, has a pod and a seal, and lacks the big motor. For a house with mostly low and medium pile, it is the sensible choice.

Inspect the gaskets every few months, wash the filters monthly and seat the pod until it clicks, because a half-seated pod leaks air. Empty the cup outdoors and rinse it now and then, letting it dry completely. A sealed machine is only sealed when the cup seats properly, so listen for the click and wipe the rim before you close it. The self-cleaning roll still collects a few strands at the bearing, so look at the ends every month, and if a household member has asthma, replace the HEPA filter on the maker's schedule, since a spent filter lets fine dust through and defeats the point of the seal. The pod nozzle is not as powerful as the main head, so use the pod for stairs and furniture and the base for rugs.
products.bestFor: Pet homes that want a seal and a pod without the premium price.

products.name: Eureka MaxSwivel Pro NEU350 with switchable brush roll

specList.label: Brush roll
specList.value: Manually controllable, can be turned off

products.description:
The NEU350 is the light, controllable option: a roll you can switch off on bare floors, dual cyclones and swivel steering with LED headlights. It is the best choice in the band for a house with hardwood and a few rugs.

Next to the Dyson it is much lighter and weaker, but it is also gentler on a polished finish. Next to the ZU561 it has the roll control but no pod or seal.

Build the habit of checking the roll switch when you change rooms, empty the cup before it fills and rinse the filter monthly. Wipe the sole plate and wheels so grit never scratches wood. The dual cyclone works best when the cup is emptied before it packs, so tip it out at about two thirds and rinse the cup now and then, letting it dry fully. Swivel steering relies on a pivot, so tilt the machine back occasionally and clear thread from the joint, and keep the headlights clean with a dry cloth, because lint on the lens dims them long before a bulb fails. Remember that the roll switch is your protection for polished wood, so make checking it a habit each time you change rooms.
products.bestFor: Mixed hardwood and rugs where control matters more than power.
cons: Easy to forget the roll setting

products.name: Eureka PowerSpeed NEU280 with upgraded cyclone

specList.label: Use
specList.value: Pet hair, carpet and hard floor

products.description:
The NEU280 is a light upright with a cyclone upgraded to handle larger debris. It is the plain, inexpensive end of the band and a good second vacuum.

Next to the Dyson it is a fraction of the weight and power, and it makes sense only if you do not need the extra. Next to the NEU350 it lacks the roll control.

Tip the cup out at the fill line, rinse the filter monthly and look over the roll for hair. Avoid running over coins and small toys, which can jam the roll. Chunky debris is hard on the bearings and the belt, so if you hear a rattle, switch off and look under the roll cover for a stuck pebble. A cyclone works best when the dirt it separates does not pack against the filter, so empty the cup a little earlier than you would a plain bin. On a deep rug go slowly and make overlapping passes, because a light head floats over thick pile instead of sinking into it, and the NEU280 is best matched to low and medium carpet and bare floors.
products.bestFor: Second vacuums and small homes with chunky debris.

products.name: Eureka PowerSpeed NEU182B, 10 lb, 2.6L dust cup

specList.label: Floors
specList.value: Carpet, shag rug and hard floors

products.description:
The NEU182B pairs a light body with a 2.6 liter cup and five height adjustments. It is the cheapest machine in the guide and a good sign that the top of the cap is not always necessary.

Next to the Dyson it has a tiny fraction of the motor, but for weekly cleaning of a small house it is enough. The cup is large for a light upright, which means fewer trips to the bin, and five heights let you tune the head to a thin rug or a bare floor. Smooth wheels help it glide, and the dynamic motor and roll lift stubborn debris, according to the maker.

Set the height when you change surfaces, empty the cup at two thirds and rinse the filter monthly. Five height settings are most useful when you actually change them: use the lowest for a thin rug, the middle for medium pile and the highest for tile or hardwood, and raise the head one notch if the machine seems to drag. A large cup is heavy when it holds sand or garden soil, so tip it into a bag held close, and check the roll for hair every few weeks, since a plain roll wraps long hair. Keep the cord wound loosely on its hooks.
products.bestFor: Small houses that want the simplest big-cup upright.

products.name: Eureka Airspeed NEU10AE4, 7.7 lb, quick-release handle
products.description:
At about 7.7 pounds the Airspeed is the lightest machine here. It is the counterweight to the Dyson: the one to buy when carrying matters more than power.

A quick-release handle converts it for above-floor cleaning with a crevice tool or a dusting brush, and the compact body stores in a closet. It is a modest machine, so thick carpet and a large home are beyond it, but for a bedroom, a hall or a small flat it is easy to carry and easy to use.

Empty the small cup after use and rinse the filter monthly. Park it standing against a wall, because a very light body tips easily, lift the head over rug edges instead of dragging it and check the roll for hair every few weeks. With so little weight pressing the head into the carpet, go slowly on rugs and make overlapping passes. Many owners buy it as a second vacuum for the upstairs, keeping a heavier machine on the main floor, and that pairing is often cheaper and more comfortable than one compromise machine.
products.bestFor: Users who need the lightest machine and clean small spaces.

buyingCriteria.explanation: The Dyson Ball Animal 3 is rated at 290 air watts, a stronger class than any other machine here. A bigger motor keeps airflow strong through thick carpet and a long session. If you have plush pile, it is the one feature that the other machines cannot match, but remember that air watts are comparable only within one maker's range, so use the figure to place the Dyson against its own siblings and not against a Shark or a Eureka that quotes a different measure.

The Dyson's de-tangling Motorbar clears hair from the bar, the Shark ZU561 has a self-cleaning roll and the Eureka models have plain rolls. Hair wrap is the common chore on an upright. At the top of the cap you can ask for a head that deals with it, and the practical test is how often you reach for the scissors: a self-clearing head turns a weekly chore into a monthly glance at the bearing ends, which is a real saving across years of ownership.

The Shark ZU561 lists a complete seal with HEPA. The Dyson is bagless and cyclonic and does not list a sealed system. For allergies the seal matters more than the motor, and a bagged sealed machine from a higher tier would serve a severe allergy better than any bagless model here, so treat these as good general cleaners and empty every cup outdoors.
The Dyson is heavy, the Airspeed about 7.7 pounds. A machine you cannot lift will not get used. Match the weight to your stairs.
The Shark ZU561 has a pod, the Dyson two accessories and the light Eurekas none. Stairs and upholstery need a tool. Count what you will use.

Under $300 you can buy one premium machine or several sensible ones. Most homes do not need the premium. Buy the Dyson only if carpet or pets justify the weight, and otherwise spend part of the cap on a light machine and keep the rest for spare belts, filters and a handheld for the stairs, which will improve daily cleaning more than a bigger motor you rarely need.

cards.text: The Dyson gives 290 air watts and a de-tangling head. It is heavy and bagless.

cards.label: Sensible
cards.text: The Shark and Eureka models are lighter and simpler. They suit most homes.

howToChoose.note: Buy the premium only if carpet or pets justify it.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A head that clears hair, a big bin and a sealed filter. Check the head monthly.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Dyson's Motorbar and the ZU561's self-cleaning roll both reduce the chore.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You have plush carpet or several pets. The Dyson's motor and head pay back.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You have low pile. The ZU561 or a Eureka does the job.

A plug looks like a weak motor.

faq.a: One premium machine or several sensible ones. The premium is the Dyson, with its 290 air watt motor and de-tangling head, while the Shark and Eureka models cover the same weekly cleaning with lighter bodies and fewer features, so decide by your carpet and your pets and not by the size of the cap.

faq.q: Does the $300 cap reflect current prices?
faq.a: The cap was applied to listing prices at the last update, and retailers reprice often, so check the live figure before you buy.

For plush carpet and pets, yes, because the motor and the self-clearing head keep working where lighter machines stall. For low pile, a Shark or Eureka is enough, and you will carry less weight up the stairs and spend less on the machine.

No. It is bagless, so emptying releases dust. Empty the bin outdoors into a bag held tight to the opening, wash the filters on schedule and consider a bagged model from a higher tier if a household member has serious allergies.

The Shark ZU561 with its complete seal and HEPA filter, because the seal keeps fine dust inside until you empty the cup. Empty the cup outdoors and replace the filter on schedule, and treat the Dyson as a strong general cleaner and not an allergy machine.

The Eureka Airspeed at about 7.7 pounds, followed by the NEU182B at about 10. Light weight comes with a smaller motor and cup, so choose it for a flat or a second floor and not as your only machine in a large carpeted home.
